name: Radish
grown_as: The summer radish, a fast annual grown for its small crisp root, ready 4 to 6 weeks from sowing. William grows a Rainbow mix (AG 116) including 'Sparkler' (round, red with a white tip), which is the one drawn, and 'French Breakfast' (long red with a white end). Left in the ground it bolts and flowers the same summer.
habit: A small rosette of leaves 10 to 20 cm high on top of a small swollen root. Bolting plants send up a branched, leafy, often bristly flowering stem 50 to 100 cm tall.

leaf.arrangement: A rosette from the top of the root; alternate up the flowering stem
leaf.type: Simple but deeply lobed: lyre-shaped (lyrate), with one large rounded end lobe and a few pairs of much smaller lobes down the lower part
leaf.outline: Long and narrow overall, 8 to 20 cm, widest near the tip
leaf.base: Tapering into the stalk, the lowest lobes small and widely spaced along it
leaf.tip: The end lobe large, broad and rounded
leaf.margin: Irregularly and bluntly toothed all round, on every lobe
leaf.veins: A pale midrib with netted side veins, one into each lobe
leaf.surface: Rough with scattered stiff bristly hairs, especially on the veins beneath and on the stalk; not waxy
leaf.stalk: Short to medium, grooved, bristly, green or flushed red

flower.petals: Four, free, each a rounded blade on a narrow claw, set in a cross
flower.colour: White to pale lilac or pale pink, with fine darker purple veins
flower.centre: Six stamens, four long and two short, with yellow anthers, round a green style
flower.behind: Four narrow upright sepals, green or purplish, close against the petal claws
flower.carried: In loose, lengthening spikes (racemes) at the stem tips, each flower on its own stalk, facing out and up
flower.season: June to September, from bolting plants

fruit: Fat, fleshy, pointed pods 3 to 7 cm long, green then straw-brown, with a long tapering beak, slightly waisted between the seeds and not splitting open. Young pods are edible.
seedling: Two broad, heart- to kidney-shaped seed leaves, notched at the tip, on short stalks, bright green; then a first true leaf that is oval, rough-hairy and toothed. Up within 3 to 5 days.
winter: Not grown over winter (summer radish); winter radishes stand in the ground into winter.

leaf: lyre-shaped: a large rounded end lobe and small widely spaced lobes lower down
bristly hairs on the stalk and veins
bloom: four rounded petals in a cross
white to pale lilac with darker purple veins
seed: a small round to slightly flattened pale brown seed, about 3 mm
seedling: two broad heart-shaped seed leaves notched at the tip, on short stalks
young: a small rosette of lobed rough leaves
a red root top starting to swell at the soil
crop: a round red root with a white base
a thin white tail root below
a short rosette of lobed leaves on top
flower: a branched leafy stem with loose spikes of pale cross-shaped flowers
fat green pods forming lower down the spikes
seedhead: fat, beaked, straw-brown pods, waisted between seeds, not split open

look_alikes: Wild radish (Raphanus raphanistrum) has a thin root, yellow or white flowers and pods strongly beaded like a necklace. Turnip seedlings look similar but are smoother. Charlock has yellow flowers.
